notes: §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR6: "Following the successful execution of a CLOSE statement without the REEL or UNIT phrase, the record area associated with a file-name-1 is no longer available. The unsuccessful execution of such a CLOSE statement leaves the availability of the record area undefined". The rule withdraws the area from the program and defines no result for a later reference (§1985:I.1.6: "The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined unless otherwise specified"), so it obliges the implementation to nothing beyond a CLOSE that completes. No edition arm: SequentialIoEmitter.EmitClose emits only the registry call and FileRegistry.CloseCell closes the connector; neither touches the record area, which is a typed field of the emitted program and keeps its last content (the realization docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-24 documents). Probed at --std 85: after a successful CLOSE, after an unsuccessful one (42), and for a file sharing its area with an open file through SAME RECORD AREA (the case 2023 defines and 1985 leaves unavailable), a reference to the area reads and stores the same storage and nothing fails. The witness closes the file after READ ... INTO and displays the saved copy (ABCDE), a conforming program that never references the closed file's area.

next.reason: 1985: 'Following the successful execution of a CLOSE statement without the REEL or UNIT phrase, the record area associated with a file-name-1 is no longer available', unsuccessful leaves it undefined, with no exception for SAME RECORD AREA. §2023:14.9.6.4 GR7 keeps both outcomes when file-name-1 is in no SAME RECORD AREA clause or none of its partners is open, but adds: 'If file-name-1 is specified in a SAME RECORD AREA clause, the record area is available to the runtime element if any of the file connectors referenced by the other file-names in that SAME RECORD AREA clause are open.' A reference through the closed file's record after CLOSE, undefined in 1985, is defined in 2023 when a sharing file is open: looser.
